extracted.intended_audience: market participants, exchanges, broker-dealers, and other interested persons who may submit comments on SEC SRO rule filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for submitting comments on a Securities Exchange Act proposed rule change (file SR-PEARL-2023-51), and standards the Commission/Staff will consider in reviewing exchange non-transaction fee filings. Covers submission methods, timing, public availability, and substantive expectations about cost-based fee proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule change effectiveness and immediate-filing treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule change "has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act, and Rule 19b-4(f)(2) thereunder."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A filing effective under Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) and Rule 19b-4(f)(2) becomes effective upon filing but remains subject to Commission review and possible summary suspension within the statutory period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission 60-day suspension power and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission may summarily temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission summarily suspends the rule change, it shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments (methods and required file number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons may submit written data, views, and arguments electronically via the Commission's internet comment form or by email to rule-comments@sec.gov; or as paper comments in triplicate mailed to the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please include file number SR-PEARL-2023-51 on the subject line. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper submission formatting and address
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper comments should be sent in triplicate to the Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions should refer to file number SR-PEARL-2023-51. The file number should be included on the subject line if email is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and availability of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will post all comments on its internet website and copies of submissions, amendments, written statements, and written communications relating to the proposed rule change will be available for website viewing and printing and for inspection and copying in the Commission's Public Reference Room on official business days between 10 a.m. and 3 p.m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include personally identifiable information in submissions; submit only information you wish to make available publicly. The Commission may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. Materials may be withheld from the public in accordance with 5 U.S.C. 552.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for comment submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should be submitted on or before October 25, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission by the stated deadline is required for consideration in the record for this proposed rule change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germane-issue expectation for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should address matters germane to the particular proposal; issues that raise larger, cross-cutting concerns with the environment surrounding exchange non-transaction fee proposals are better addressed through Commission rulemaking or Congressional action rather than an individual exchange filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange stated that where a commenter attempts to raise new issues not germane to this particular proposal, those issues should be addressed more holistically (e.g., via rulemaking) rather than in an individual fee filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to statutory standards under the Exchange Act (Section 6/15 U.S.C. 78f(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule changes must be consistent with the Exchange Act, including provisions of 15 U.S.C. 78f(b) (and specifically subsections cited such as 78f(b)(4), 78f(b)(5), and 78f(b)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those statutory provisions include requirements such as preventing unfair discrimination (6(b)(4)), protecting investors and the public interest and promoting just and equitable principles of trade (6(b)(5)), and not imposing burdens on competition not necessary or appropriate (6(b)(8)). Filings should be framed to demonstrate consistency with these statutory factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Guidance and Revised Review Process expectations for fee filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Staff Guidance on SRO Rule Filings Relating to Fees (May 21, 2019) and the Revised Review Process inform the Commission Staff's expectations for fee filings, including requests for more detailed cost and revenue disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange notes that since 2021 Staff frequently requests detailed cost information and that Staff has applied (or indicated) a more detailed review standard for non-transaction fee filings; filers should be prepared to develop a record and explain conclusions in a written decision sufficient to enable Staff review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-based fee proposal disclosure expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: When pursuing a cost-based approach to fee filings, exchanges should provide detailed cost and revenue disclosures; the Exchange requests that such disclosures be consistent across exchanges for fair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange argues the Commission should issue substantially more detailed guidance for exchanges to follow in pursuing cost-based fee filings and that disclosures provided to Staff (including vendor cost information) may be subject to confidentiality restrictions and provided under separate cover with a confidentiality request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential treatment for vendor/third-party cost information
rubrics_metrics.description: Vendor cost information that is subject to confidentiality restrictions may be provided to Commission Staff under separate cover with a request for confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange has provided such information to Staff under separate cover and expects to continue responding to Staff requests while seeking consistent disclosure standards across exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to explain cost allocation methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Filers should justify how costs are allocated (for example between equities and options platforms, or across matching engines, gateways, directors, and market data feeds) when asserting costs supporting fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange provides examples discussing allocation differences (e.g., number of matching engines, gateways, or amounts spent on proprietary market data feeds) and notes other exchanges' more granular allocations; filers should explain allocation choices to enable Staff review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection and explanation of profit margins and related assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filers proposing fees based on cost should identify projected profit margins and explain the assumptions underlying those projections (including sensitivity to inflation or other economic changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange notes that Staff determinations may include judgments about appropriateness of profit margins and suggests Staff should be clear about what they determine is an appropriate profit margin; filers should disclose projected margins and assumptions (e.g., inflation impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural expectation if Commission takes summary action
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission summarily suspends a rule change within the 60-day window, it will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should be aware that summary suspension triggers formal proceedings and an expanded opportunity for record-building and briefing.
